title: When Arise the Thoughts of Sin
description: When Arise the Thoughts of Sin in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 148, “Christ Who Strengtheneth Me”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: When a-rise the thoughts of sin, When the world our hearts would win, When, to self-ish plea-sure given, Droops the love that blooms for heaven; Lord, we would re-mem-ber thee, Thou wilt our Re-deem-er be.

lines: When arise the thoughts of sin,
When the world our hearts would win,
Droops the love that blooms for heaven;
When, with footsteps faint and slow,
When, by toils and hardship pressed,
Round we turn to look for rest;
Thou our Guide and Strength wilt be.
When the way grows dark and drear,
When, beset by doubt and fear,
We can see no beam of light

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
